messages:
Tom (support): FYI customer 'AcmeAnalytics' on private VPC is seeing lots of 429s on our gateway during short bursts. They say it started after they rolled out a batch job that hits the inference endpoint concurrently from a few dozen pods. Error spike ~11:05 UTC, lasting intermittent bursts for ~10s every minute. 429s are from our gateway (X-RateLimit-Reason: ingress_burst).

Aisha (support): Can you paste the gateway error snippet/logs and the customer's K8s ingress config? Need to know if they're using our customer-managed gateway or our packaged envoy helm. Also any info on retries from client side?

Tom (support): Logs: 
```
[2026-03-15T11:05:43Z] gateway: req_id=abc123 path=/v1/generate status=429 reason=ingress_burst token_bucket=true remote_ip=10.0.5.12
[2026-03-15T11:05:44Z] gateway: req_id=abc124 path=/v1/generate status=503 downstream_overloaded
```
Ingress config (they posted): 
```
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: acme-inference
  annotations:
    kubernetes.io/ingress.class: nginx
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-connections: "200"
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-rpm: "1000"
spec: ...
```
They also run an envoy sidecar (customer-managed) -> we saw envoy config points to local ratelimit service with global domain "redwood-rate" and descriptors by cluster.

Aisha (support): Good. Two likely issues: (1) client-side retries + lack of retry-backoff causing burst amplification; (2) mismatch between K8s ingress limits and gateway token-bucket settings — ingress allows connection burst but gateway enforces token bucket per-customer which floods 429 when many concurrent connections map to same bucket.

Ben (SRE): Quick triage checklist:
- Confirm whether gateway uses a per-ip or per-client token bucket. If per-client and many pods share same client id, they'll contend.
- Check envoy/local rate-limit service logs for descriptor hits.
- Look at kube-proxy conntrack / NAT exhaustion if many ephemeral ports.
- Reproduce with a controlled burst. I usually run `wrk` or a small k6 script to simulate pods.

Maria (eng): If they're on our customer-managed gateway, recommend one of these config paths depending on their tolerance: 
1) Increase bucket capacity (burst) and refill rate sustainably. Example token bucket params we expose: `rate: 100 rps, burst: 300` for short-lived spikes.
2) Apply per-source (pod IP) token buckets instead of single tenant-wide bucket. That distributes burst.
3) Add a short client-side retry-jitter and exponential backoff (disable naive immediate retries).

Suggested envoy ratelimit YAML snippet for reference:
```
rate_limit_service:
  domain: redwood-rate
  descriptors:
  - key: PATH
    value: "/v1/generate"
  - key: CLIENT_ID
    value_from_header: "x-client-id"
```
And token-bucket settings in gateway config: 
```
rate_limits:
  default:
    unit: second
    requests_per_unit: "30"   # baseline
    burst: "120"
```
Note: increasing burst avoids immediate 429s but can raise steady-state cost if sustained.

Tom (support): Customer says they don't set x-client-id (many internal services call without it). They use k8s DNS hostnames; pods are NATted through node IPs so many show same source IP. Might explain contention.

Aisha (support): If pods are NATted behind node IPs, per-source-IP won't help. Options: require/insert client-id header at sidecar or ingress, or enable per-token (API key) buckets. Can we ask them to inject a header via the ingress? Example nginx annotation to add header: `nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/configuration-snippet: 'proxy_set_header x-client-id $pod_ip;` Not ideal but helps distribution.

Ben (SRE): Also check kube-proxy mode. If they're using iptables and a lot of ephemeral connections, conntrack table might thrash. Run: `sudo conntrack -S` or `kubectl exec -n kube-system kube-proxy -- conntrack -L | wc -l`. If conntrack limit reached, you'll see timeouts and 5xx.

Tom (support): They ran a quick `kubectl exec` and saw conntrack at ~120k/128k limit. They bumped kernel `net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max` to 262144 for now.

Maria (eng): Good mitigation. For longer-term: either move to keep-alive connections (reduce ephemeral ports) or add local envoy upstream pooling. Also set our gateway to honor a higher `connection_drain_threshold` so sudden pod churn doesn't create bursts.

Aisha (support): Practical mitigation steps to propose to customer (order matters):
1) Short term (apply now): increase conntrack on nodes + increase gateway burst to 120-300.
2) Immediate configuration: have ingress inject x-client-id (unique per pod) or use a sidecar that sets a per-pod header.
3) Client changes: implement jittered exponential backoff on retries; cap total retries.
4) Long term: move to per-source token-buckets keyed on x-client-id or API key; consider Dedicated capacity if traffic patterns need high short bursts.

Tom (support): Customer accepted 1+2. They asked for exact commands to patch nginx ingress to add header and example gateway values.

Maria (eng): Example patch for nginx ingress (annotation):
```
metadata:
  annotations:
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/server-snippet: |
      proxy_set_header X-Client-Id $request_id;
```
This uses `$request_id` generated per-request — not ideal. Better: sidecar that sets X-Client-Id to pod name at egress, e.g., init container writes env var and sidecar adds header.

Ben (SRE): Example gateway curl to test behavior and induce burst (run from a pod):
```
for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' http://gateway.internal/v1/generate &
done
wait
```
Then tail the ratelimit service: `kubectl -n redwood logs -l app=ratelimit --since=2m` and watch descriptor hits.

deploy-bot: rate-limiter-service restarted by deploy pipeline at 11:22 UTC (deploy/rls-2026-03-15-11-22).

Aisha (support): After applying conntrack bump + ingress header injection + gateway burst increase to `burst: 200`, customer reported immediate drop in 429s. They still see occasional 429s under extreme single-second floods, but overall success rate much higher. They will implement client retry jitter and sidecar for client-id next week.

Tom (support): I'll send a summary + runbook to the customer and recommend a follow-up in 48 hours to consider moving them to Dedicated if spikes persist and they want SLA guarantees. Also flagged for billing: their naive retries generated higher tokens consumed — advise on quota alerts and cost caps.

Maria (eng): Add a note: if they move to per-client_id buckets, ensure descriptors are cached in local ratelimit (avoid RPC on every request) — we have a caching knob `descriptor_cache_size`. Default 1024 might be too small for many distinct clients.

Ben (SRE): I'll add a short internal postmortem checklist to the thread for future similar tickets (conntrack, ingress header, bucket keying, retry patterns). cc @oncall for knowledge share. :memo:

Tom (support): Thanks everyone. Closing loop with customer now, will log ticket updates. :white_check_mark:
